_comment: CRITERION OVERRIDES for the frozen BYOK border-design corpus (track byok_svg_borders_20260927).
A per-design `criterion` normally comes from the round file that WON the freeze (last-
accepted-wins), so the criterion a design is judged by is the one its frozen bytes were
generated for. That invariant is deliberately OVERRIDABLE, by an operator ruling: when a
criterion is re-cut WITHOUT regenerating the artwork (the bytes stay the winning round's),
the freeze takes the criterion from THIS file and records both texts on the fixture entry
(`criterion` = the override, `criterionGenerated` = the round file's text,
`criterionOverride` = the provenance). The override file is a freeze INPUT, so a fresh
freeze over the same rounds + this file is still byte-reproducible.
FOUR overrides exist. D-C and R-3 are operator rulings made 2026-10-01 before any further
gate run (`phase4_operator_rulings_20261001.md` §1 D-C,
`phase4_operator_rulings_r2r3_20261001.md`). R-6 and R-7 are the operator's 2026-10-02
instruction to RE-CUT (rather than re-freeze) the two canonical designs whose criteria name
features the pipeline cannot paint; their measured basis is filed as
`phase4_round25_recut_evidence.md`.
D-C — 04-dragon-scale's scale rows are judged aspect-independently because the product's
`border-image` edge scaling is ANISOTROPIC on a tall section (~0.146 px/unit horizontal vs
~0.923 vertical with `round` on 656x1920), so square scales become vertical slivers on the
left/right rails while the top/bottom rails keep the source's own proportions. The render
knob did NOT move; the criterion did.
R-3 — 01-gilded-frame's criterion demanded a GOLD tone, which the product's own default
decoration filter (`grayscale(100%)` at the shipped defaults, applied to every border kind
through the same `::before` slot) makes unsatisfiable by construction: measured on the
judged frame, gold-classified pixels 0.0000% on the TOP band while the frozen blob's gold
#c9a227/#d4af37 renders as the luma-161 grey the band measures. Under operator ruling R-2
(the judged instrument stays at PRINT defaults), the criterion is re-cut to the SHAPES the
pipeline actually paints — measured on the same frame: two concentric rules continuous on
every edge (TOP 96.9%/95.7%, BOTTOM 95.5%/96.9%, LEFT 98.9%, RIGHT 98.6-99.0% line
coverage; the only break runs are the corner junctions where the perpendicular rules meet,
which is the ring's own structure, not a dash pattern) and a diamond-shaped corner mark at
each of the four corners (ink inside the diamond box the frozen blob's own coordinates
predict: 113/94/104/91 px against 72 px in an identical control box on the same rails —
R-6 / R-7 — the RE-CUT pass (operator instruction 2026-10-02). Both designs' criteria name
features that are NOT reachable by any pipeline stage, so no artwork could satisfy them:
the `border-image` pipeline paints only the source's EDGE SLICES, so a shape drawn in the
middle of the source viewBox is cropped away before any pixel exists. 05-celestial-arcs' six
four-pointed stars sit at source y 52..168 of a 256-tall viewBox and 07-corner-arcs' nested
quarter-arcs sit in its four source CORNERS — the region that slice painting replaces with
the slice's own corner artwork is not composed from the design's, and the judged instrument's
band strips are edge strips, so a corner is outside every strip it takes. Measured on the
judged native cells (`phase4_round25_recut_evidence.md`): 05's TOP band carries 19 separate
ink components (635 px, 0.81% of the band) at depth 50..55 of 56 device px, i.e. thin marks
along the band's inner line and no star shape anywhere in the band; 07's FOUR corner boxes
(28x28 CSS at the section's own corners, which the band strips do not cover) carry 4.69/3.35/
2.81/3.35% ink against 05's 1.91/0.00/0.00/0.00%, i.e. 07's corner groups ARE painted and are
the only place they appear.
Both re-cuts name what the judged frame MEASURABLY carries and record the unreachable demand
as such, so a MET here is a statement about the frame, not a waiver. The artwork was NOT
regenerated (the operator chose re-cut over re-freeze); the frozen bytes are unchanged and
the unreachable decorations are recorded as residuals of the two designs.

04-dragon-scale.criterion: Overlapping scale shapes are drawn in rows along the border, each scale visibly tucked under or over its neighbour; the individual scales are judged where the pipeline paints them at the source's own proportions — the top and bottom rails — and the left and right rails must carry the same overlapping-row texture even where the pipeline's anisotropic edge scaling narrows the individual scales.
04-dragon-scale.supersedes: Overlapping scale shapes are drawn in rows along the border, each scale visibly tucked under or over its neighbour, and the rows read as the same texture on the left/right as on the top/bottom.
04-dragon-scale.reason: Operator ruling D-C: the frozen 4c blob (800x800, filled paths) is deformed by anisotropic border-image edge scaling on the 656x1920 gallery section; the ruling re-cut the criterion aspect-independently and kept the render knobs unchanged, so the criterion now judges the source's proportions where the pipeline preserves them and only demands texture (not aspect) on the anisotropic rails.

01-gilded-frame.criterion: Two concentric rectangular rules run as continuous SOLID lines along every edge — each rule unbroken from corner mark to corner mark around the full rectangle, no dash pattern and no mid-edge break in either rule — and both rules are present on all four edges, with a diamond-shaped corner mark at each of the four corners. The rules are judged by SHAPE, continuity and doubling only: the product's default print filter renders the whole band in greyscale, so no hue is expected in the judged frame and an absence of colour is NOT a failure of this criterion.
01-gilded-frame.supersedes: Two concentric rectangular rules in a gold tone are both drawn as continuous SOLID lines closed around the full rectangle — no gaps or dashes anywhere on either rule — a diamond mark sits at each of the four corners, and no rule crosses the interior.
01-gilded-frame.reason: Operator ruling R-3 (paired with R-2, which keeps the judged instrument at the product's PRINT defaults): the frozen round-5b blob strokes `url(#goldGrad)` #c9a227/#d4af37, and a clean-Chromium reproduction of the shipped border-image pipeline paints that band gold (8.3% gold px), but the product's own default decoration filter — `grayscale(100%)` at the shipped defaults, applied to every border kind through the same ::before slot — removes the hue before any pixel exists. Measured on the judged native cell, the band is the greyscale of the authored gold (luma 161) and gold-classified pixels are 0.0000% on the TOP band; a colour-demanding criterion is therefore unsatisfiable by construction for ANY artwork, not just this one. The ruling re-cuts the judged TEXT to the shapes the pipeline does paint — two concentric rules continuous on every edge plus a corner mark at each corner, both measured on the judged frame — and keeps the frozen bytes (sha256 99605fc3…, round 5b) unchanged.

05-celestial-arcs.criterion: Thin solid arc strokes are painted as an unbroken line along the top edge and along the bottom edge, and the SAME arc treatment is carried on the left and right edges; every stroke is a plain solid line — no dash pattern and no broken or fragmented run anywhere on the frame. The arcs are judged by SHAPE and continuity only. The design's four-pointed star marks are NOT part of this criterion: they are drawn in the middle of the source viewBox, which the product's `border-image` slice painting crops away before any pixel exists (measured on the judged frame: 0 star shapes in any band; the sole ink in the TOP band is a thin mark at the band's inner line), so no artwork of this design can show them and their absence is NOT a failure of this criterion.
05-celestial-arcs.supersedes: A thin arc curve drawn as a single unbroken solid stroke (no dashes, no gaps) runs along the top edge and along the bottom edge, and at least four separate four-pointed star shapes are visible in the space between them.
05-celestial-arcs.reason: Operator instruction 2026-10-02 (re-cut rather than re-freeze). Measured basis filed as `phase4_round25_recut_evidence.md`: the frozen round-5 blob draws its two arcs at source y 8..24 / 232..240 of a 256-tall viewBox — inside the top and bottom slices, which the pipeline paints — and its six star polygons at source y 52..168, i.e. in the middle of the viewBox, which `border-image` slice painting never paints. On the judged native cell the TOP band's ink is 19 separate thin components totalling 635 px (0.81% of the band) at band depth 50..55 of 56, with no star geometry anywhere; the criterion's star clause was therefore unsatisfiable by construction for ANY artwork of this shape, exactly as R-3's gold clause was. The re-cut keeps the frozen bytes (sha256 bce88831…, round 5) and records the star marks as a residual of the design.

07-corner-arcs.criterion: Nested quarter-circle arc groups are painted in the border's CORNERS — each of the four corners of the framed section carries a group of nested arcs, the nesting direction is consistent at all four corners, and the corner groups are joined along each edge by straight rules that run between them. The corners are judged where the pipeline paints them, at the section's own corners (the 28x28 CSS box at each corner of the framed rectangle); the criterion does not require the corner groups to be visible inside an edge strip, because an edge strip does not cover a corner. Arc count and nesting are judged by SHAPE only.
07-corner-arcs.supersedes: Each of the four corners shows at least three nested quarter-circle arcs, the nesting direction is consistent at all four corners, and straight rules connect the corner groups along each edge.
07-corner-arcs.reason: Operator instruction 2026-10-02 (re-cut rather than re-freeze). Measured basis filed as `phase4_round25_recut_evidence.md`: the frozen round-4 blob's four nested-arc path groups live in the source's own four corners (its path data starts at 8,136 / 216,136 / 8,8 / 216,8 of a 224x144 viewBox) and its four straight `line` elements join them along each edge. On the judged native cell the four corner boxes at the section's own corners carry 4.69% / 3.35% / 2.81% / 3.35% ink — against a control design (05) measuring 1.91% / 0.00% / 0.00% / 0.00% at the same coordinates — so the corner groups ARE painted and are the only place they appear; the EDGE strips the previous criterion was read against do not span a corner, which is why the clause as written was unjudgeable rather than unmet. The re-cut keeps the frozen bytes (sha256 84f10f25…, round 4) and moves the judged location to the corners the design actually paints.
